title: Least-privilege read-only Postgres role for diagnostics and reporting

sha_binding.verified_source_note: Implementation commit on branch claude/utv2-1633-readonly-postgres-role, pre-PR. Rebound to the real squash-merge SHA post-merge by post-merge-lane-close.yml via ops:proof-generate --merge-sha, per the same allowance UTV2-1399 used.

verifier.identity: read-only measurement against production Supabase zfzdnfwdarxucxtaojxm and staging xskgrzbteyqdufktjrjx via Supabase MCP execute_sql, 2026-08-01
verifier.method: Every claim about live database state is quoted alongside the exact SQL that produced it. All statements executed against either live database are SELECT only; no DDL was applied and no row was created, updated, or deleted by this lane.
verifier.verifier_scope: This identity verifies (a) that schema `reporting` and role `reporting_reader` do not yet exist in production or staging, (b) the pre-existing PUBLIC/schema-level privilege baseline in production, and (c) that the migration's own static/local checks pass. It does NOT verify the role's actual read/write behavior against a live database, because the role does not exist in either environment yet -- see verification.md 'BLOCKED' section.

grant_statements: GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE postgres TO reporting_reader;
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA reporting TO reporting_reader;
GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA reporting TO reporting_reader;
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA reporting GRANT SELECT ON TABLES TO reporting_reader;

role.name: reporting_reader
role.attributes: NOLOGIN NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOREPLICATION NOBYPASSRLS
role.note: Creating and proving this role's privilege boundary is this lane's full scope. Granting it to a login/service credential or replacing an existing credential with it is a separate governed production action requiring explicit PM authorization, per the issue's own 'Governed rollout' section.

measurement.after_state_note: Blocked -- reporting_reader and schema reporting do not exist in production or staging. See verification.md 'BLOCKED' section for the exact unblocking action.

static_proof.guard_intent: Mechanically enforces: reporting_reader is NOLOGIN with every role-administration attribute explicitly denied; every GRANT/ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES statement targets only schema reporting with only SELECT/USAGE/CONNECT, never INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE/CREATE/ALL, and never schema public or any public.* relation; the migration fails closed if schema reporting is missing; the migration verifies its own grant set in-transaction before committing; the rollback drops the role and revokes every grant without touching schema reporting itself; the migration creates no schema object of any kind other than the role.

reversibility.rollback_restores_prior_behaviour_exactl: DROP OWNED BY reporting_reader + explicit REVOKEs remove every privilege this migration granted; DROP ROLE IF EXISTS removes the role itself. Schema reporting and its views (owned by UTV2-1399) are never touched -- the rollback asserts this in-transaction.
reversibility.round_trip_drill_note: No Docker or psql available locally. migration-reversibility-gate.yml replays the full migration ledger (including UTV2-1399's, which precedes this one by timestamp) on scratch postgres:16, so schema reporting exists in that drill regardless of production's current state. That drill's schema-hash comparison uses --schema=public --no-acl, which captures neither roles/grants nor schema reporting, so this migration is expected to be schema-hash-neutral there.
